_comment: The five hazards of human spaceflight defined by NASA's Human Research Program. 'summary' is a short paraphrase of the official page (shown in the UI, English). Short names live in config/strings.en.json as hazard.<id>. Which indicators watch each hazard comes from indicators.json 'hazards'.

hazards.summary: Space radiation is invisible to the human eye and is considered one of the most hazardous parts of spaceflight.
People isolated and confined in a small space for a long time show behavioral responses; crews must work as a team for months or years.
The farther the crew travels, the harder it is to get instructions, supplies and medical care from Earth.
Muscles, bones, inner ear and organs must adjust to each new gravity field: weightlessness, the Moon, Mars, and Earth again on return.
A closed spacecraft must keep temperature, pressure, lighting and noise right, and monitor microbes and immune responses.
